Franchise
The phased migration to the new Voter.ie, which is being led by the Electoral Modernisation Project Team in
Dublin City Council, is now underway commencing with the four Dublin local authorities who completed their
migration on 25  May 2026 following the local by-election. All other local authorities will migrate over the coming
months and it is anticipated that all local authorities will be using Voter.ie to manage their electoral registers by the
end of 2026. 
th
Voter.ie is being delivered as part of the Electoral Reform Act 2022 to provide a single, national electoral
registration system that enables local authorities to effectively fulfil their duties as registration authorities.  Voter.ie
will provide a streamlined online application process offering both MyGovID and PPSN authentication.
In the interim checktheregister.ie will remain active for those wishing to register or check their details and as each
local authority migrates, users will be automatically redirected to the new system.
Waterford City & County Council are currently scheduled to go live on Voter.ie on the week of 14  September. The
process of preparing for migration to Voter.ie has required a significant level of input from the Franchise Team as
part of the Local Government Electoral Reform Scheme (LGERS) Project outlined in the infographic below.

Economic Development
NORTH QUAYS
Works on the sustainable transport bridge are well progressed
with the installation of the edge railings, glass panels and
pedestrian barriers.  The remaining finishing works, e.g.
surfacing, lighting, street furniture will proceed over the
summer along with the final commissioning of the automated
systems for the opening span, the removal of temporary river
piles and the completion of the permanent pier protection
system. 
It should be noted that Harcourt Development, as part of their
planning permissions are required to deliver a podium to tie
directly into the new Sustainable Transport Bridge. The podium
will allow pedestrians and cyclists to move seamlessly into the
North Quays and will provide access to the residential and
commercial elements of the development.
The South Plaza will provide a landscaped public realm area
with seating, lighting, green areas and bicycle facilities.  Works
are complete apart from final paving detailing, cycleway
surfacing, snagging checks and audits, in advance of the full
area being made open to the public.  Public access from the
South Plaza to the sustainable transport bridge will be closed
off and secured until the bridge opens to the public in 2027.   
 
Finishing works are continuing to the train station building, this
includes mechanical & electrical fitout, installation of flooring
and second fix joinery and finishes to offices, toilets etc.  
Access lifts are also currently being installed.  The testing &
commissioning of the various operational systems in the
station will proceed in the coming months. The construction of
the southern entrance of the transport hub will also
commence in the coming months.  
Page 8 of 43
2
External works to the north of the train station are also close to completion, this includes the northern plaza/ public
realm, set-down area and layby. It provides facilities for cars, buses and taxis and bicycles. 
Iarnród Éireann will complete the installation of new trackside signalling, electrical and telecoms equipment
through 2026 and into Q1 of 2027. The completion of these separate works/processes will facilitate the opening of
the train station towards the end of 2027.  The completion of the railway flood defences (see below) is also required
before the station can open.

NORTH QUAYS
All infrastructural works on Dock Road, Fountain Street
and Abbey Road are complete and snagging, safety audits
will be completed in June for the final certification of the
works. The greenway ramp at Abbey Road will facilitate
the sectional opening of the 6km section of greenway
from Abbey Road to Curraghmore by Wexford & Kilkenny
County Council’s.  
 
The overall railway flood defence scheme is progressing.
The installation of the river sheet pile wall for the western
flood defence scheme is now complete, while the eastern
flood defence scheme and the eastern trackside drainage
scheme are also complete. A contract has been awarded
for the western trackside drainage scheme which will
commence in the coming weeks.   
 The central flood defence works through Plunkett Station
will proceed in late 2026. The works are complex and
logistically challenging as they will progress through the
station car parks, entrance and set-down areas. The site is
very spatially confined and the works are being planned
to ensure safety while also minimising disruption to rail
services and commuters. The project team continues to
consult with Iarnród Éireann on the logistics for these
works and the best means of reducing impacts and costs.
Flood defence pumping stations will also commence
works in 2026. The overall railway flood defence scheme
will be completed in 2027 to facilitate the opening of the
new transport hub and associated new rail infrastructure.

‘Oh my Cookies’ wins LEO Pitch Perfect competition
Oriana Ramirez with her business ‘Oh my Cookies’ is the
successful 2026 Waterford Pitch Perfect business. ‘Oh
My Cookies’ creates New York style cookies, cookie
bars, and cookie cakes in a fun and indulgent way.
Within the past year Oriana has grown her business from
an interesting hobby to selling in cafes, online and at
markets all over the south east. Apart from her baking
skills and imagination, her real point of differentiation is
her marketing and presentation skills.
Local Enterprise Office (LEO) Waterford, SETU Xcelerate Centre and Boxworks Co Working Space joined forces to
deliver this Start Up Competition for those with an innovative business idea or those already in business trading
less than 18 months.
Participants, limited to those based in Waterford, were guided through the initial stages of developing their
idea/business. Then successful applicants were selected for a Business Boot camp where they perfected their
pitch before presenting to panel of judges.
The bootcamp was delivered by the Entrepreneurs Academy across two Saturdays, May 16th and 23rd. The
winner received €1,000 in prize money. All participants were offered mentoring as part of our LEO Mentoring
programme.

Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) update
The RZLT Final Map 2026 was published by Waterford City and County Council on 31  of January. This map
identifies lands that are liable for payment of the tax for the tax liability year 2025, The final map is available to
view on the consult.waterfordcouncil.ie portal page. 
st
In addition to the above, the RZLT Annual Draft Map 2027 has also been published on
consult.waterfordcouncil.ie on the 1  of February. During the initial public consultation period which ran to
April 1 , a total of eight written submissions were received to both maps, two of which have requested the
rezoning of lands in Waterford City while six have sought to have the lands removed from the scope for the
tax. Following our consideration of these submissions, potential land rezoning will form part of variation no. 2
of the city and county development plan, a process which will be commenced over the coming summer
months. Making any changes to the land use zoning provisions of the development plan will be a reserved
function of the elected members. 
st
st
Expressions of Interest call for Residential Development Land
Further to our recent public campaign to identify suitable lands for new residential development which was
hosted on the consult.waterfordcouncil.ie consultation portal, at time of writing a total of seven written
submissions have been received. We will assess the content of all submissions received prior to the 5  of June
to prepare the content of variation no. 2 of the city and county development plan which is due to be
commenced over the summer period. Rezoning of land arising from the RZLT process in the current year will
also form part of the variation. In addition, the variation will include settlement capacity audits, surface water
management plans, local transport plans and integrated town development strategies. The content of the
variation will be workshopped with the plenary council in advance of commencing the formal development
plan variation process.

The team is currently addressing 434 properties, classified as either derelict or potentially derelict. In recent weeks
and months, there has been a significant increase in activity, with 151 properties now listed on the Derelict Sites
Register. Engaging with property owners or their representatives is essential to addressing dereliction issues and
understanding the numerous factors contributing to the properties' current condition. 
The level of activity in the property market concerning vacant and derelict properties has notably increased. Among
the properties we have identified as derelict, several have been voluntarily reintroduced to the private market, with
some currently at the 'sale agreed' or 'to let' stages. 
We are actively engaging with the new owners of these properties to ensure they are fully informed of their
obligations under the Derelict Sites Act 1990. We are also seeing a consistent number of planning applications for
property refurbishment/extension, and the level of work ongoing on individual properties is clear when driving
around the city and county. 
We are notifying property owners about the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant, designed for properties that can
be converted for residential use. Additionally, the Vacant Above the Shop Grant provides up to €95,000 to help
convert unused space above commercial premises into homes. These grants have significantly boosted the number
of derelict and vacant properties now available on the market. Applicants for these grants can receive financial help
for timely submissions, enhancing the appeal of property revitalisation.
Through effective collaboration among property owners, financial institutions, and various departments, we can
create positive pathways for the redevelopment and revitalisation of many derelict sites.

was again undertaken and is greatly complemented by the ‘City of Light’ initiative. Specific festival gobos were
again on display with festival messaging and thematic images. These effects offered a unique self-guided tour
experience with historical monuments and city walls illuminated in green, background historical information on the
buildings was available via an interactive online map. A significant P.R. campaign was managed by Visit Waterford
